relevance_note: Case report of one child with compound heterozygous ITGB2 variants: "The WES result demonstrated a compound heterozygosity for two variants in the ITGB2 gene".
method_note: Read by hand; JSON assembled with a short Python script from hand-chosen spans. In scope: the case patient; her parents (both underwent WES, results for them not stated, so no variant rows and inheritance 'not reported'); her younger full sister (WES negative for both ITGB2 variants, so no variant rows); 'ref (13) patient' (previously published LAD-I patient homozygous for c.314T>C, Discussion); 'ref (14) patient' (19-year-old with LAD-I treated with ustekinumab, Discussion). The paper says the patient has 'one full sibling' and that the younger sister shares both parents, so these are probably the same person; not merged and 'healthy' not attached to the sister. Out of scope: three healthy untested half-siblings; 'several unrelated patients' homozygous for c.817G>A (refs 5, 28) with no individual-level detail; group statements from the literature review. Age at onset uses the age at first presentation ('16-month-old'); no age at diagnosis or last evaluation is given for the patient. c.817G>A pathogenicity left 'not reported': the paper only cites 'pathogenic/likely pathogenic by three independent submitters' and in silico scores, not its own classification. 'concern for poor wound healing of the I&D site' is hedged, so impaired wound healing was left 'not reported'. 'ear infection' as a flare trigger was not mapped to otitis media. 'Cardiopulmonary and abdominal exams were unremarkable' recorded as written (whole-exam normal, excludes nothing more specific). Table 1 values (no flags in the table) were not interpreted except NADPH oxidase activity 'Normal'. Patient 'parental consanguinity: no' also applied to the sister (same parents). No contradictions found.
